project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 301 (System combines promoted signals by information-ratio weighting, which returns a single composite target score per symbol)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 301 in a new `book` plugin (packages/book, import name book; seat src/app/modules/book): a pure combiner that takes the promoted signals — each carrying its out-of-sample information ratio and one target score per symbol — and returns a single composite target score per symbol, weighted by each signal's information ratio. The sentence's verb is `combine(signals)`: it reads each promoted signal's information ratio and its per-symbol target scores, weights signal i by w_i = IR_i (the information-ratio weighting the sentence names), and answers a composite score per symbol equal to the weighted average of that symbol's scores across the signals that carry it — `composite[s] = Σ_i w_i · score_i[s] / Σ_i w_i`. The information ratio is a signal's standing to weight the book, so a signal presenting a non-positive or non-finite ratio is refused rather than zero-weighted or dropped (silently discarding a losing signal would hide a portfolio decision); a signal that expresses no score for a symbol the book covers is refused rather than zero-filled (absence is not a view, the stance the marginal-IR step takes on a book signal that misses a priced date); and an empty set of signals is refused because a book of zero signals has no composite. The answer is a frozen `CompositeBook` that carries the composite target score per symbol beside the weight and information ratio each signal carried, so the composite is checkable against its own terms — the record discipline feature 83's MarginalIR and feature 256's WorldScore both keep. It is a pure function of evidence the factory does not hold (the promoted signals), so it registers as a callable component named `book` — the combiner itself, contributed once and consumed by whoever composes, exactly the shape scoring's `world_objective` takes — and the seat (src/app/modules/book) answers *what is the composed book combiner?* for a caller that holds the app namespace. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; the member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member — the promoted signals arrive as this member's own `PromotedSignal` value, validated field by field, across the same "no member imports another" seam the scoring and regime members take.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (new `book` member, packages/book, import name book; seat src/app/modules/book) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package; the book seat (src/app/modules/book) answers *what is the composed book combiner?* for a caller that holds the app namespace, the way the scoring seat answers *what is the composed per-world objective?*.

existing_context.conventions: - One act, one module: `_combine.py` holds the combiner verb, the `PromotedSignal` input value, the `CompositeBook` answer and the refusal vocabulary; `errors.py` carries the base error class; `__init__.py` re-exports the public names, registers the `book` callable component, and carries no logic — the shape every member in this workspace takes. - A callable component, the scoring precedent: the `book` component is the combiner itself (`combine`), not a store or a service. It has no `DATABASE_URL` to be absent and no environment to read; its whole configuration is the arithmetic (the information-ratio weighting, restated here rather than imported from the evaluator or scoring member — a member never imports a member). The builder `build_book_combiner()` takes no arguments and returns `combine` unchanged, never raising; a composed application therefore carries the one callable the order layer reaches through the app package to turn the promoted signals into a composite ranking. - The seat answers one question and no more: *what is the composed book combiner?* It asks the factory for the `book` component and returns the `combine` callable (or `None` when the member was not scanned — a statement about composition, not an error, and a caller that finds `None` must refuse to rank rather than re-derive the arithmetic beside it). It does not re-export `PromotedSignal`, `CompositeBook` or the error vocabulary: a caller who has the callable calls it and gets the value, and a second spelling of the member's surface here would be a second thing to keep in sync — the discipline the scoring seat states, and the reason the member's suite pins this module to exactly the names it carries. - The promoted signal is this member's own frozen value: `PromotedSignal(signal_id, information_ratio, target_scores)`, with `signal_id` a non-empty name, `information_ratio` a finite real, and `target_scores` a non-empty mapping of symbol to a finite score. `combine` validates each field it reads (a member that constructs the value the caller hands it still checks what it receives — the "validate what you read" rule); the value is frozen because a promoted signal is a recorded fact a later edit must not be able to re-weight without re-deciding the promotion. - Information-ratio weighting is the sentence's one mechanism and is a convention, not a knob: signal i's weight is `IR_i`, and the composite is the weighted average `Σ_i IR_i · score_i[s] / Σ_i IR_i`. It is not a caller's parameter — a weight is a portfolio decision, and the combiner's job is to apply the one weighting the spec names, so two deployments report the same composite for the same signals. (Downstream features — 302's covariance shrinkage, 303's volatility targeting — take this composite and rescale it; they do not re-open this weight.) - Absence is not zero, twice over: a signal with a non-positive or non-finite information ratio is refused (its standing to weight the book is undefined, not zero); a signal that carries no score for a symbol the book covers is refused (it expresses no view on that symbol — zero-filling would counterfeit one). Neither is defaulted. - Full coverage: every signal must carry a score for every symbol the book covers (the union of the signals' symbol sets), so the composite over a symbol is the weighted average across *all* the signals — the stance feature 83's marginal IR takes on a book signal that misses a priced date (refused, not zero-filled). A signal missing a symbol is refused naming the signal and the symbol, before any composite is formed. - The composite is checkable against its own terms: `CompositeBook` carries the composite score per symbol, the normalized weight each signal carried (summing to one), and each signal's information ratio, and construction enforces that every composite score equals the weighted average of the contributing scores under the carried weights — the self-consistency MarginalIR enforces on its ratios and the node-metrics store on its `ic_mean`. - Error vocabulary opens with a greppable code: `BookConstructionError` is the base, and every refusal message opens with a one-word code (`empty_book`, `unnamed_signal`, `duplicate_signal`, `non_positive_ir`, `non_finite_ir`, `signal_without_scores`, `non_finite_score`, `uncovered_symbol`), the `pool_frozen` / `unwalkable_tree` precedent, so an operator greps one word for the refusal. - Deterministic and order-independent: the composite is a sum over signals and so does not depend on the order they arrive; symbols are emitted in sorted order so two calls over the same signals answer identical `CompositeBook` values. No clock, no environment, no store, no third-party import at module scope — stdlib only (`dataclasses`, `math`, `collections`), so the factory's scan pays nothing and the combiner is import-cheap on the replay path. - Do not edit a central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration (core-task, order-sensitive shared files); the member joins by workspace-scan convention and registers its `book` component with `@register` from its own `__init__.py`.

feature.description: System exposes `combine(signals)`, the book combiner: it takes the promoted signals — each a `PromotedSignal` carrying its out-of-sample information ratio and one target score per symbol — weights signal i by `w_i = IR_i` (the information-ratio weighting the sentence names), and returns a single composite target score per symbol, the weighted average of that symbol's scores across the signals, `composite[s] = Σ_i w_i · score_i[s] / Σ_i w_i`. The information ratio is a signal's standing to weight the book, so a signal presenting a non-positive or non-finite ratio is refused rather than zero-weighted or dropped; a signal that expresses no score for a symbol the book covers is refused rather than zero-filled (absence is not a view); and a set of zero signals is refused, because a book of zero signals has no composite. The steps, in the order they must happen: (1) collect the signals into a list, refusing an empty set (`empty_book`) and a signal with no `signal_id` (`unnamed_signal`) or a `signal_id` already seen (`duplicate_signal`); (2) validate each signal's `information_ratio` is a finite real and strictly positive, refusing `non_finite_ir` and `non_positive_ir` naming the signal; (3) validate each signal's `target_scores` is a non-empty mapping of symbol to finite real, refusing `signal_without_scores` and `non_finite_score` naming the signal (and the symbol, for the latter); (4) resolve the symbol set as the union of the signals' symbols and require every signal to carry a score for every symbol in it, refusing `uncovered_symbol` naming the signal and the symbol before any composite is formed; (5) form the total weight `W = Σ_i IR_i` and each normalized weight `w_i = IR_i / W`; (6) form each symbol's composite as the weighted average of its scores under the normalized weights; (7) answer a frozen `CompositeBook` carrying the composite score per symbol, the normalized weight per signal and each signal's information ratio, with construction enforcing that every composite equals the weighted average of its contributing scores. A refused combine forms no value.

System defines `PromotedSignal`, the frozen input value the combiner takes — a promoted signal's recorded fact. It carries three fields: `signal_id` (the signal's non-empty name — the promotion record's identity for it, stripped non-empty text, never normalised away, so a signal that names nothing is refused as `unnamed_signal`); `information_ratio` (the signal's out-of-sample information ratio, the scalar the promotion gate admitted it on — a finite real, and the weight it will carry; carried as given and validated strictly positive at combine time, not here, so the value is a plain record and the policy lives in the verb); and `target_scores` (a non-empty mapping of symbol to the signal's target score for that symbol — the signal's per-symbol view, each a finite real). Frozen, for the same reason `MarginalIR` and `WorldScore` are: a promoted signal is the record of a decision, and a caller who could edit its ratio or its scores in memory could re-weight the book without re-running the promotion that earned the signal its place. A symbol that is not text, or a score that is not a finite real, is refused at construction — the value admits only what the combiner can score, so a malformed signal is caught where it is built, not where it is combined. Construction is observable: a `PromotedSignal` built with a blank `signal_id`, a NaN ratio, or a non-finite score raises `BookConstructionError` (the value rejects what the combiner could not score), and the member's suite asserts the frozen value carries the three fields unchanged for a well-formed signal.

System answers `CompositeBook`, the frozen composite — the single ranking the combine verb returns. It carries the composite target score per symbol (`scores`, a mapping of symbol to the weighted-average score, emitted in sorted-symbol order so two calls over the same signals answer identical values), the normalized weight each signal carried (`weights`, a mapping of `signal_id` to `w_i = IR_i / Σ_j IR_j`, summing to one), and each signal's information ratio (`information_ratios`, a mapping of `signal_id` to `IR_i`, the raw standing the normalized weight reduces from), and it exposes `target_score(symbol)` returning the composite score for one symbol. Frozen, because the composite is the order layer's ranking and a value that could move after it was read would be a ranking that changed beneath the instruction that consumes it — the same guarantee `WorldScore` makes for a world's score. Construction enforces self-consistency: every `scores[s]` must equal `Σ_i weights[i] · score_i[s]` recomputed from the carried weights and the contributing per-symbol scores, and every weight must equal `IR_i / Σ_j IR_j` recomputed from the carried ratios — the defence MarginalIR applies to its ratios and the node-metrics store to its `ic_mean`, so a `CompositeBook` is a check rather than a claim and a hand-built one whose composite is not its own weighted average is refused. All scalars are finite reals — NaN and ±inf are refused on both the scores and the weights, so no fabricated infinity ranks above an honest score.

System exposes `BookConstructionError`, the combiner's refusal vocabulary — one base class, every message opening with a greppable one-word code (the `pool_frozen` / `unwalkable_tree` precedent), so an operator greps one word for the refusal. Its faces, each naming the signal (by `signal_id`) and, where relevant, the symbol: `empty_book` — `combine` was handed no signals, so there is nothing to weight into a composite; `unnamed_signal` — a signal carries no `signal_id` (a blank or absent name), so it has no identity a weight could be attributed to; `duplicate_signal` — two signals carry the same `signal_id`, so a weight could not be attributed to one signal; `non_positive_ir` — a signal's information ratio is zero or negative, so its standing to weight the book is undefined (refused rather than zero-weighted, because silently dropping a losing signal would hide a portfolio decision); `non_finite_ir` — a signal's information ratio is NaN or ±inf, which would reach the composite dressed as a standing; `signal_without_scores` — a signal carries an empty `target_scores`, so it expresses no view to contribute; `non_finite_score` — a signal's score for a named symbol is NaN or ±inf; and `uncovered_symbol` — a signal carries no score for a symbol the book covers, so it expresses no view on that symbol (refused rather than zero-filled, absence not being a view). The code is the first token of every message, and the signal and symbol are named so the refusal is actionable without a stack trace; a `combine` handed any of these raises `BookConstructionError` with the coded message and returns no `CompositeBook`, which the member's suite asserts by checking the raised message begins with the code.

System registers the combiner as the callable component `book` and seats it in the app package. The `book` member's `__init__.py` declares `COMPONENT_NAME = "book"` and a builder `build_book_combiner()` — decorated `@register(COMPONENT_NAME)`, taking no arguments, reading no environment and never raising — that returns `combine` unchanged, so a composed application carries the one callable the order layer reaches through the app package to turn the promoted signals into a composite ranking; the combiner's whole configuration is the arithmetic, so it cannot misconfigure or degrade, exactly the property scoring's `build_world_objective` states for the objective. The seat (src/app/modules/book) answers *what is the composed book combiner?*: it asks the factory for the `book` component and returns the `combine` callable, or `None` when the member was not scanned — a statement about composition, not an error, and a caller that finds `None` must refuse to rank rather than re-derive the arithmetic beside it. The seat does not re-export `PromotedSignal`, `CompositeBook` or `BookConstructionError`: a caller who has the callable calls it and gets the value, and a second spelling of the member's surface here would be a second thing to keep in sync — the discipline the scoring seat states. The member's suite asserts the component name and the seat's accessor agree, so the two spellings of one name cannot drift.

System passes an end-to-end combine: three promoted signals, each with a strictly positive information ratio and a target score for each of a shared symbol set {BTC, ETH, SOL}, combine to a `CompositeBook` whose `scores` hold one composite target score per symbol, whose `weights` sum to one and rank the signals by information ratio, and whose `target_score(symbol)` returns the weighted average of the three signals' scores for that symbol — and a re-run over the same signals in a different order answers an identical `CompositeBook` (the composite is a sum and so is order-independent, and symbols are emitted sorted). Refusals, each leaving no value: a signal with `information_ratio = 0.0` is refused as `non_positive_ir` naming the signal (not silently dropped); a signal with `information_ratio = float("nan")` is refused as `non_finite_ir`; a signal whose `target_scores` omits SOL is refused as `uncovered_symbol` naming the signal and SOL (not zero-filled); a signal with an empty `target_scores` is refused as `signal_without_scores`; two signals sharing a `signal_id` are refused as `duplicate_signal`; and an empty signal set is refused as `empty_book`. The composite is checkable: each `scores[s]` equals `Σ_i weights[i] · score_i[s]` recomputed from the carried weights, so the record is a check rather than a claim.

project_specification.integration_points: The combiner is a pure function of evidence the factory does not hold (the promoted signals), so it registers as the callable component `book` — the combiner itself, contributed once and consumed by whoever composes, exactly the shape scoring's `world_objective` takes (`build_world_objective` returns `world_objective` unchanged under the component name `scoring`). The seat (src/app/modules/book) reaches that component through the factory, the way the scoring seat reaches the objective. The member imports no other workspace member: the promoted signals arrive as this member's own `PromotedSignal` value, and the information-ratio weighting is restated here rather than imported from the evaluator member (feature 83's `compute_marginal_ir`) or the scoring member (feature 80's `_information_ratio`) — a member never imports a member, and the one spelling of the information ratio this combiner uses (mean over population standard deviation) is pinned here in its own terms. Downstream features take this composite as their input: feature 302's covariance shrinkage stabilizes the weight vector, feature 303's volatility targeting rescales it, and feature 305 returns the final target weights the order layer consumes — but none of them re-opens the information-ratio weighting this feature fixes. No `@register` name collides (the component is `book`, distinct from every existing member), no table, endpoint or migration is added, and no central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited.
project_specification.constraints: - No member imports another: the promoted signals are this member's own `PromotedSignal` value; validate `signal_id`, `information_ratio` and `target_scores` field by field, and the information-ratio weighting is restated here, never borrowed from the evaluator or scoring member. - One callable component named `book`, registered with `@register` from the member's own `__init__.py`; the builder takes no arguments, reads no environment and never raises, and returns `combine` unchanged. - The seat answers exactly one question — *what is the composed book combiner?* — returns the `combine` callable or `None`, and re-exports nothing else from the member. - Do not edit a central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration (core-task, order-sensitive shared files). - Information-ratio weighting is the sentence's one mechanism and is a convention, not a knob: `w_i = IR_i`, composite the weighted average; not a caller's parameter. - Absence is not zero: a non-positive or non-finite information ratio is refused (not zero-weighted), and a signal missing a symbol is refused (not zero-filled); full coverage is required — every signal must carry a score for every symbol the book covers. - Validation is total before any composite is formed: an empty set, an unnamed or duplicate signal, a non-positive or non-finite ratio, an empty or non-finite score map and an uncovered symbol are all refused before the total weight is summed, so a refused combine forms no value. - The composite is checkable: `CompositeBook` carries the composite score per symbol, the normalized weight per signal and each signal's information ratio, and construction enforces that every composite equals the weighted average of its contributing scores under the carried weights. - Deterministic and order-independent: the composite is a sum over signals; symbols are emitted sorted; stdlib only (`dataclasses`, `math`, `collections`) and import-cheap at module scope. - Every refusal message opens with its greppable code, and names the signal (and the symbol, where relevant), so the refusal is actionable.

phase.name: Feature 301 — combine promoted signals by information-ratio weight
phase.step: 1. Create the `book` member: `packages/book/pyproject.toml` (a uv-workspace member, stdlib-only, src layout with import name `book`), and declare it in the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members` alongside the existing members so the module loader's scan discovers it.

2. `packages/book/src/book/errors.py`: the base `BookConstructionError(Exception)`, documented to open every message with a greppable one-word code and to name the signal (and symbol, where relevant).

3. `packages/book/src/book/_combine.py`: `PromotedSignal` (frozen dataclass: `signal_id`, `information_ratio`, `target_scores`, with `__post_init__` validating non-empty text id, finite-real ratio and a non-empty symbol→finite-real mapping); `CompositeBook` (frozen dataclass: `scores`, `weights`, `information_ratios`, with `target_score(symbol)` and a `__post_init__` that enforces each composite equals the weighted average of its contributing scores and each weight equals `IR_i / Σ_j IR_j`, refusing a self-inconsistent or non-finite record); and `combine(signals)`, which runs the seven ordered steps in the act bullet and answers the `CompositeBook`. Stdlib only.

4. `packages/book/src/book/__init__.py`: re-export the public names (`combine`, `PromotedSignal`, `CompositeBook`, `BookConstructionError`), declare `COMPONENT_NAME = "book"`, and register `build_book_combiner()` under `@register(COMPONENT_NAME)` returning `combine` unchanged. `py.typed` marker. Assert in the member's suite that the exported surface is exactly these names.

5. `src/app/modules/book/__init__.py`: the seat — ask the factory for the `book` component and return the `combine` callable (or `None`), answering *what is the composed book combiner?* and re-exporting nothing else. Document the `None`-means-not-scanned semantics and the refuse-don't-re-derive stance.

6. Tests: `packages/book/tests/test_combine.py` (the act — the three-signal happy path, order-independence, the checkable composite, and every refusal face — `empty_book`, `unnamed_signal`, `duplicate_signal`, `non_positive_ir`, `non_finite_ir`, `signal_without_scores`, `non_finite_score`, `uncovered_symbol`); `packages/book/tests/test_component.py` (the `build_book_combiner` builder returns `combine` and never raises, the `book` component composes through `create_app`, and the seat returns the callable). `packages/book/tests/conftest.py` bootstraps the member onto `sys.path` the way the sibling members' conftests do.

7. Validate and run the member's own suite (the repo-level suite under tests/ does not collect packages/*/tests — run the member suite explicitly), and lint only the new files against a sibling baseline.

project_specification.success_criteria: - `combine` over three promoted signals (positive IR, shared symbol set) returns a `CompositeBook` with one composite target score per symbol, weights summing to one and ranking by information ratio, and a re-run in a different signal order answers an identical value. - Every composite score equals the weighted average of the contributing per-symbol scores under the carried weights (the record is a check). - Each refusal — `empty_book`, `unnamed_signal`, `duplicate_signal`, `non_positive_ir`, `non_finite_ir`, `signal_without_scores`, `non_finite_score`, `uncovered_symbol` — fires on its face, opens its message with the greppable code, names the signal (and symbol), and forms no value. - A non-positive or non-finite information ratio is refused, not zero-weighted; a signal missing a symbol is refused, not zero-filled. - The `book` component composes through `create_app()` and the seat returns the `combine` callable (or `None` when the member is absent). - The member is stdlib-only at module scope and import-cheap; the factory's scan pays nothing. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; no table, endpoint or migration is added.
